purpose: Core-language Alpha functional acceptance contract. This file declares requirements and does not assert a passing candidate or a published release.
target: Linux x86_64 native applications and libraries
compile_time_programming: Ordinary source generation and immutable ready-stage type queries preserve full current type, scope, dependency and budget identities; unavailable stages reject rather than fabricate an empty type domain.
acceptance_unit: One real cross-module Source program and its relevant error, cleanup and nearest safety-negative cases complete the entire compiler and execution chain in the same exact candidate. Compiler-stage components or separately passing branches do not constitute a delivered feature.
required_chain: Source elaboration preserving original semantic declarations and actual emission identities
Types materialization into complete canonical Typed types and real instructions
Independent Verify of current raw/Wire input and actual capability obligations
Clang and LLVM API execution at O0 and O2
Observable results, failure handling and exact resource cleanup
joint_coverage: Type/Const/Life generics and associated/default methods combined with ordinary owned and borrowed values
Closures, captures, helpers and container iteration preserving complete type and lifetime domains
Actual selected heterogeneous providers and their real sources, effects and teardown
Task inputs/results/captures through Pending, Ready, replacement, cancellation and close
Language-defined collections, text and I/O used through the ordinary project workflow
compatibility: No positive compatibility obligation for historical schema, internal IR or unreleased APIs. The current format rejects unknown/obsolete versions. Historical evidence remains archived; current safety counterexamples and real Source inputs remain required.
delivery: A single exact source candidate with non-author review, complete nonzero functional coverage, reproducible build/run/test instructions and a clean independent restoration is required before publishing Alpha.
separate_claims: Alpha functional acceptance does not claim complete 1.0 generalization, Rust-relative performance ratification, ZUI/GPU/IME completion or native execution on untested platforms. Their existing gates remain in force.
